newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up in sluggish trade.

text.p: * Gainers number the same as losers
Manila shares closed slightly up in quiet trade on Wednesday as most investors opted to stay on the sidelines due to the Christmas season, traders said.
"We followed Wall Street's rise but trading was pretty quiet on the broad front as focus was on specific stocks," said Louie Bate, head of sales at ING Barings Securities.
The main index ended up 12.59 points, or 0.41 percent, at 3,105.80.

San Miguel shares led the rise among blue chips ending 3.50 pesos higher at 56.50 a share. "Local bargain hunters are just recognising the value of A shares against the B shares which closed unchanged," Bate said.
Gainers and losers were evenly matched at 53 each with 79 issues unchanged.
Though trading on the floor was thin and lacklustre, volume was above average at 2.718 billion pesos due to block sales, traders said. All sectors rose except for the property sector.
"We may see more of the same tommorrow as there's no news to perk the market up," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.
Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities, said the market was expected to drift for the rest of the week because most investors had started their Christmas holidays.
